messages:
incident-bot: Pager duty alert: elevated 5xx rate from gateway cluster eu-west-1. Triggered by 30%+ error spike over 3m, paging oncall @alice oncall :rotating_light:

alice oncall: seeing 502/504s on frontend dashboards. Customers report timeouts and long tails. I'm on it, paging @bob-sre for infra assist.

bob-sre: joining. Graphs show error rate started at 10:08 UTC, coincident with a gradual increase in kv-prefix cache evictions across prefix-shards-3a and -3b.

carol-runtime: FYI we rolled a small eviction-tuning patch to prefix cache at 09:58 (canary on 3a/3b). It bumped aggressive eviction scoring; I suspected it might be aggressive but tests looked fine.

dave-se: customer impact from Support: multiple customers hitting streaming timeouts and a few 502s. Support ticket numbers: #4582, #4583. Erica, can you flag customer comms?

erica-pm: acknowledged, drafting a status note.

alice oncall: quick mitigation proposal: 1) revert eviction-tuning on canary nodes, 2) enable kv read-through bypass to origin for high-miss prefixes, 3) throttle prefix-shard prefetching to reduce load.

bob-sre: running live checks.

bob-sre: logs from shard agent (excerpt):
```
[2026-03-15T09:59:12Z] WARN kv-prefix: eviction_loop: scored=0.98 prefix=usr_12345 items=1024 -> evicting bulk 512
[2026-03-15T09:59:13Z] ERROR kv-client: stream_write failed: io timeout (502 proxy)
[2026-03-15T09:59:14Z] WARN prefetch: queue_len=1200 backlog=30ms
[2026-03-15T09:59:17Z] ERROR gateway: upstream 502 on PUT /v1/generate
```

carol-runtime: that matches the rollout window. I'm preparing a quick rollback job: kubectl rollout undo deployment/prefix-cache-canary --namespace=runtime-canary - to restore the previous eviction scoring.

alice oncall: bob, can you limit prefetch concurrency on 3a/3b? config flag is PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=4 (was 16).

bob-sre: applying now via feature-flag:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" https://ops-api.internal/featureflags/prefetch-concurrency -d '{"value":4,"namespaces":["prefix-shard-3a","prefix-shard-3b"]}'
```

bob-sre: set to 4, observed immediate drop in backlog metric. error rate dipped slightly.

dave-se: any live routing fallback we can enable to reduce customer impact (e.g., route reads to dedicated read-through cluster)?

carol-runtime: yes, enabling origin fallback for cold-prefix hits. This will bypass prefix cache reads and go direct to persistent KV for misses. Enabling for prefixes with miss-rate>0.3. Command:
```json
{ "action": "enable_bypass", "selector": "miss_rate>0.3", "ttl_override_s": 5 }
```

carol-runtime: sent patch to config service, change should roll in <30s.

bob-sre: after bypass toggle, 502s reduced by ~60% on canary. 504s still present but tail improved.

alice oncall: good. Start customer communications: acknowledge degradation, note mitigation steps and ETA for full rollback. Erica please post.

erica-pm: posted to status.redwood.ai: "We are investigating elevated errors in EU region due to cache eviction behavior; mitigations in progress. No data loss. Updates every 30m."

dave-se: is there any risk enabling bypass for stateful workloads? Could increase origin load and trigger paging there.

bob-sre: origin RT increases expected. Mitigation: apply temporary rate-limiting on non-critical paths and reserve headroom on origin pool. Spinning up two origin read replicas in eu-west-1 now (autoscale request sent).

carol-runtime: rollback initiated for eviction-tuning on canary nodes. Command:
```bash
kubectl -n runtime-canary rollout undo deploy/prefix-cache-canary --to-revision=3
```

carol-runtime: rollback completed at ~09:16 UTC, verifying.

bob-sre: metrics after rollback + prefetch throttle + bypass: error rate down to baseline within 6m. Current 5xx volume: 12% above normal (was 220%).

alice oncall: leaving oncall to @bob-sre for next 30m for stabilization, I'll stay available. @bob-sre you're primary for incident table.

bob-sre: taking over. Actions remaining: 1) run kv-prefix sanity scan to check for corruption, 2) audit eviction counters to ensure no silent rot, 3) plan conservative rollout with lower evict thresholds.

bob-sre: running quick integrity check:
```bash
# sample check
for shard in prefix-shard-3a prefix-shard-3b; do 
  ssh $shard "/usr/local/bin/prefix-check --scan --sample 1000" > /tmp/${shard}_scan.log &
done
```

bob-sre: sample output shows occasional checksum mismatch on a small subset (~0.02%):
```
prefix-shard-3a: checksum_mismatch count=2 keys=[usr_987, usr_543]
prefix-shard-3b: checksum_mismatch count=1 keys=[usr_222]
```

dave-se: small mismatch set. Could be transient due to eviction race. Suggest marking affected prefixes for manual rebuild and add stronger checksum validation in next patch.

ercia-pm: (typo in participants) meant erica-pm above.

erica-pm: noted. I will coordinate customer follow-ups for the prefixes we've flagged.

bob-sre: marking keys for rebuild and scheduling background repair job:
```bash
repair-tool --shard prefix-shard-3a --keys usr_987,usr_543 --priority low
repair-tool --shard prefix-shard-3b --keys usr_222 --priority low
```

carol-runtime: I'll open a PR to add a safety backoff to eviction scoring and a kill-switch for rapid revert. Also adding telemetry to surface eviction burst anomalies in the Console.

alice oncall: post-incident checklist: root-cause hypothesis = over-aggressive eviction scoring (new tuning patch) exposed an eviction-thundering pattern on hot prefixes which increased upstream gateway timeouts and 502s. Contributing factor = lack of a fast rollback path and insufficient preflight load tests on canary.

bob-sre: incident severity reduced. Will keep monitoring for 60m and then file handoff doc.

erica-pm: customer-notes update: initial mitigation applied, rollback completed, repairs in progress, next update in 30m.

alice oncall: handing off to oncall rotation notes: @bob-sre primary until 10:30 UTC, escalation to @carol-runtime for any runtime rollbacks.

bob-sre: acknowledged. Closing pager for oncall. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. Incident ID: INC-20260315-evictwave-1775001234. Timeline and logs will be archived to the incidents folder.

alice oncall: quick postmortem items: add automated canary load test covering eviction churn, add an automated circuit-breaker to pause eviction scoring changes on spike, improve runbook for prefix-bypass fallback. I'll create tasks after incident.

bob-sre: uploading collected artifacts: /var/logs/incidents/1775001234/*.tar.gz

carol-runtime: PR link: https://git.internal/r/runtime/pulls/432 - adds kill-switch + backoff.

erica-pm: prepping customer summary and internal postmortem draft.

alice oncall: thanks everyone. Closing thread after stabilization window.
